Sports.title: The task facing Mykhailo Mudryk after his 20-month ban: Rio Ferdinand hit the ground running for Man United, Paul Pogba's fitness woes and Diego Maradona's mixed spell in Spain after their lengthy suspensions
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk's long-awaited return to football came on Tuesday as Chelsea winger came on as a late substitute in their friendly against Juventus.

Mudryk's brief cameo – a 10-minute appearance – came after his doping ban came to an end this week after a resolution was reached with the Football Association.

The £89million signing had not played since November 2024, when he started and scored away at Heidenheim in the Conference League, after he had been suspended from football after failing a doping test for the banned substance meldonium.

Daily Mail Sport revealed this week that Chelsea have already been approached by clubs to ask about their plans for Mudryk this season.

Whatever outcome is reached, there is an understanding patience will be required with Mudryk having been out of the game for 20 months.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at previous examples of how other players have got on after returning to the game from long bans from football.

Mykhailo Mudryk made his return to football this week after his 20-month doping ban ended

Clubs are interested in a move for the Chelsea winger with an acceptance he will need time to return to his best after 20 months out of the game

Rio Ferdinand – Eight-month ban

The task facing Mudryk is outlined by Ferdinand's comments after returning from his doping ban in September 2004.

'Physically and mentally is was all new again, eight months out is a long time,' Ferdinand said after making his return.

Ferdinand had been hit with an eight-month ban from football and a £50,000 fine back in 2003. He had been sanctioned after failing to provide a drugs sample following a training session on September 23 that year.

His ban officially began in January 2004, starting days after he had been forced off injured during Man United's 1-0 defeat by Wolves.

Ferdinand, who failed in an appeal against his ban in March, was forced to watch from the sidelines as Man United suffered a dip in form in his absence and ultimately missed out on retaining their Premier League title. The ban also forced him to miss Euro 2004.

He ultimately made his return in September, with Sir Alex Ferguson throwing Ferdinand straight into the starting line-up as Man United hosted rivals Liverpool at Old Trafford.

Ferdinand required an energy bar to help him through the match, having not been able to play in friendlies to get him back up to speed.

Rio Ferdinand returned from an eight-month ban in September 2004 for Manchester United

Ferdinand played the full 90 minutes on his return as Man United earned a 2-1 win over Liverpool

Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Ferdinand's performance as 'superb' in their victory

Ferguson hailed his performance as 'superb' and highlighted how Ferdinand's composure had helped his side, as Man United earned a 2-1 win courtesy of two Mikel Silvestre goals.

'The fans were fantastic as soon as I came out for the warm-up and even after they were brilliant,' Ferdinand told Sky Sports post-match.

'It is just nice to get out there and play, you forget about everything that has gone on beforehand but once you get out there and start warming up and game starts, it is all about football.

'It was never going to be easy, I was under no illusions that I was going to have an easy game. It was nervous energy, I needed some sugar intake and the physio brought around a little bar to chew on. It was obvious needed, eight months is a long time.

'I am not looking back, I am looking forward and continue playing football now and do what I love doing.'

Having made a stuttering start to the season by winning of their opening five matches, Man United's form picked up after Ferdinand's return to action with the defender also immediately earning a recall to the England squad.

Ferdinand was close to being an ever-present for Man United after his return to action, missing just two league matches in the remainder of the campaign.

Eric Cantona – Eight-month ban

One of the most famous bans in football history was handed to Cantona after he kung-fu kicked a Crystal Palace supporter in January 1995.

The Frenchman had launched himself into the crowd having reacted to goading from one supporter, following his red card in the match.

Man United initially suspended Cantona until the end of the season, but the Football Association ultimately extended his ban for eight months.

Cantona returned in stunning fashion on October 1 as Man United faced Liverpool, with home fans at Old Trafford turning up to the clash with French flags adorning his face to mark his comeback.

Eric Cantona was famously banned for eight months after kung-fu kicking a Crystal Palace fan

Cantona scored and assisted in his return as Man United drew 2-2 with Liverpool in 1995

The Man United talisman made an instant impact by setting up Nicky Butt for the opening goal. With Man United having then fallen behind, Cantona then scored from the penalty spot to secure a 2-2 draw.

'It's Eric's stage, Eric's the lead actor and Eric delivers the best lines,' Man United forward Brian McClair reflected to Sky Sports.

'It was as if he'd never been away,' added Steve Bruce. 'It was quite incredible that somebody who had been away for so long could come back and have the impact he did straight away, and it lifted everybody.'

Cantona proved the inspiration for Man United to complete a league and FA Cup double. The Frenchman top scored with 19 goals in all competitions including netting against Liverpool in the FA Cup final, a match where he captained the Red Devils.

He was named as the Football Writers Association's Player of the Season.

Adrian Mutu – Seven-month ban

Mutu was part of the Roman Abramovich led revolution at Chelsea in 2003, with the Romanian among ten players the Blues splashed out on that summer.

The £15.8million signing scored ten goals in 36 matches during his debut season at the club after joining from Parma.

Mutu would ultimately fall out with his new manager Jose Mourinho at the start of the following season amid concerns over his lifestyle. Mutu then tested positive for cocaine use in September 2004 and was handed a seven-month ban from football.

Chelsea sacked the forward as a result with the Blues chasing £15.2million in compensation.

'Taking cocaine during my time at Chelsea was the worst decision I could have made in my career,' Mutu reflected in an interview last year.

'I was alone and sad, but neither depression nor anything else justified my actions. Zero tolerance – that was Chelsea's policy regarding drugs. And I think that's fair.

Adrian Mutu had been one of Chelsea's high-profile signings of the early Roman Abramovich era

Mutu was sacked by Chelsea after a positive test for cocaine, and the club then demanded he paid £15.2m in compensation

The Romanian forward spent a season at Juventus, before rebuilding his career at Fiorentina

'I made a mistake, strayed from the path, and paid the price for it. I was caught off guard. I wasn't used to that life. I was unprepared.

'I arrived at Chelsea during a turbulent time in my personal life, and I found myself caught up in too many excuses and lies. I was too young and too alone.

'I've reflected on that many times. I believe that for more than a season, I was amongst the best players in the world, so I could have won it easily. But bad decisions prevented me from doing so. I try not to beat myself up about it.'

Mutu was handed an almost immediate chance to return to the game with Juventus signing him in January 2005, despite his suspension running until May.

He scored seven goals in 32 league matches the following season as the Old Lady won Serie A – before later being stripped of their title.

Mutu moved on to Fiorentina in the summer of 2006 and spent five seasons at the club, scoring 54 goals in 112 league appearances. This led to Mutu being inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2024.

The forward had served a nine-month ban in 2010 after a failed doping test.

Paul Pogba – 18-month ban

Pogba's case represents an interesting comparison to Mudryk's owing to the similar length of time out of the game.

The French midfielder, like Mudryk, was initially facing a four-year ban from football with Pogba having tested positive for the prohibited substance DHEA in September 2023, when he was playing for Juventus.

His suspension was later reduced to 18 months following an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Pogba told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

The former Man United star was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance.

The World Cup winner, however, had already endured a series of injuries during his second spell at Juventus and Pogba's time on the sidelines during his ban also left him playing catch up.

Monaco had given Pogba his own fitness plan and planned to gradually introduce him into the team following his long absence.

Paul Pogba signed for Monaco last summer and viewed the move as a second chance after his 18 month doping ban ended

Pogba, however, spent much of the season on the sidelines amid a series of fitness issues

The 33-year-old managed just 115 minutes last season with Monaco considering his future

The 33-year-old ultimately played just 115 minutes for the Ligue 1 side last season as he struggled for fitness and form, with Monaco considering whether to part ways with him this summer.

Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro said last month: 'It is a complicated topic because we have a lot of respect for Paul, for the person he is. Since he arrived, he has been very positive.

'It is also true that, last year, the project didn't work well because when we started with him in the summer, the expectations were very different to what happened. I think that we have to be fair with him, follow his preparation every week, how he will progress physically and technically and then it will be the manager's decision.

'We have the summer to see what level we will see from Pogba. He could [leave at the end of the summer]. With Paul, it has always been a very open and transparent relationship.

'If, at some point, the expectations of the player are different to the expectations of the club, we will have to speak to find a solution. The performance will give all the answers that we need. Maybe he will stay, maybe he will leave.'

Diego Maradona – 15-month ban

The legendary Argentine was banned from football for 15 months back in 1991 after testing positive for cocaine.

The sanction effectively ended his historic spell at Napoli, who he had inspired to win two league titles, the Copa Italia and UEFA Cup.

Maradona looked to rebuild his career at Sevilla after his ban came to an end, as he joined forces with Carlos Bilardo, who had been Argentine's coach for their 1986 World Cup triumph.

His arrival proved lucrative for Sevilla with the club holding marquee friendlies during pre-season, with the club said to have enjoyed a £2.5million uptick in revenues during his sole year at the club.

Diego Maradona spent a season at Sevilla after serving a 15-month suspension from football

Maradona was initially seen as having a positive impact at the club, despite being overweight after the prolonged spell out of the game. Maradona, who was given the captain's armband after signing, helped the club into the top three of the LaLiga table early on.

The 32-year-old also produced an inspired performance in a 2-0 victory over Real Madrid.

His off-the-field problems, however, derailed Maradona during the second half of the season, leading to Sevilla hiring a detective to track him.

A falling out with Bilardo also contributed to Maradona spending just a single season at Sevilla, who finished seventh in the league, before he returned to Argentina.

Sports.title: Alleged scammer who 'targeted NFL players in million-dollar scheme' found dead in swimming pool at 24
Sports.content:
The alleged mastermind of a million-dollar scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool.

An investigation has been launched into the death of Mohamed Coulibaly, 24, after his body was discovered at a house in Harrison Township, New Jersey.

According to ABC, police officers visited the home after family members expressed concerns about Coulibaly.

Only last month, the 24-year-old from Philadelphia was named by Barron's as the organizer of an alleged scam that attempted to lure ex-NFL players and other athletes into buying a stake in 'bogus websites.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly allegedly hoped to dupe the athletes into believing they were investing in successful businesses. Instead, three ex-NFL players claimed to have lost more than $1million combined.

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was former New York Giants linebacker Tae Crowder. He reportedly invested his life savings - worth $500,000 - into one of Coulibaly's ventures.

The alleged mastermind of a scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was ex-New York Giants star Tae Crowder

'We were just, every day, talking about different investments and different things we could possibly get into. I saw him hanging out with a bunch of different guys that I know, which you know made me feel comfortable,' Crowder recalled, per ABC.

'I would log into the store all the time and just see how it would work and what was going on. I feel like the more I told him about that, as many times I kept logging in, the number started going up.'

But Crowder claims he never saw any return on his investment. 'I don't want anybody else to get involved in anything like this, and whoever has got involved, I just want to come together and make it right.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly claimed investors had not received any money because he was still waiting for funds himself.

At the time of his death, ABC reports, no criminal charges had been filed related to the alleged scheme.

A GoFundMe page, purportedly created by Mohamed's brother, Badra, has raised nearly $13,000. The family is 'urgently working to bring him home so he can be laid to rest with dignity and peace.' Coulibaly previously told Barron's that he immigrated to the US as a child with his Malian family.

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne heads to Shergar Cup believing big wins ‘prove career has not plateaued’
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne heads to Shergar Cup believing big wins ‘prove career has not plateaued’

The 24-year-old will make her second appearance at Ascot’s Dubai Duty Free-sponsored team event as captain of the Britain and Ireland team

View 3 Images Saffie Osborne: team captain at the Shergar Cup (Image: Dave Benett)

Saffie Osborne hopes her 2026 successes have proved she is on a path towards a future challenge for the jockeys’ championship.

‌



The 24-year-old will captain a Britain & Ireland team of Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle, both former or present champions, at tomorrow’s Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot.

‌



Osborne has climbed to seventh in the jockeys standings with 40 wins this season while her prize-money earnings exceed her 2024 best, thanks to high profile victories in the Weatherbys Super Sprint and Moet & Chandon International.

‌



“Anyone that starts off in this job, not wanting to be champion jockey, shouldn't be doing it because it's so tough and gruelling that if you're not aiming to be at the top, then I don't know why you're really doing it, to be honest,” she said.

Ffos Las race meeting moved to earlier start time to avoid effects of solar eclipse READ MORE :

“In 2024 I rode a large number of winners, but I lacked riding a top quality horse, which is starting to come now.

“Then last year I was just plagued with problems. I got injured twice and I had to cut my season short just as it started to get going again.

‌



“It just felt like nothing was kind of clicking into the right place and then in the back of your mind you're hoping you haven't plateaued or reached the level of where you're going to be. I think this year has proved that's not the case.”

View 3 Images Saffie Osborne: enjoying her best season in the saddle (Image: Dave Benett)

She went on: “It started brilliantly in May when I think I had 20 winners, and it's just gone from strength to strength since. My weight has been so good this year, and that's been a huge help. I've managed to ride so many good horses for really great connections.”

‌



Osborne has a formidable record at Ascot, where she rode two winners on her only previous Shergar Cup appearance, landed her first Group winner at the track and rode a treble on King George day to take her total haul at the course to 21.

“I have had a lot of luck there outside of the Royal meeting,” she said. “Maybe it’s because I’ve been going there since I was in a pram.”

The Shergar Cup features some of the best in the world with Frida Valle Skar and Marie Velon joining Lemaire for Europe, Jerry Chau and Luke Ferraris teaming up with Ho for Hong Kong and India’s Suraj Narredu and legend Yutake Take alongside Melham.

‌



View 3 Images Shergar Cup riders (r-l) Yutaka Take, Jamie Melham, Suraj Narredu, Christophe Lemaire, Luke Ferraris, Jerry Chau

Riders have been allocated rides by drawing lots for all six handicaps with points are awarded from 15 for winning, through 10, seven, five and three for fifth place, with Osborne’s best chance of a win from her five looking to be 7-4 shot Hoseki for William Haggas in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic.

As team skipper Osborne is looking to emulate Jamie Spencer as the last captain of Great Britain and Ireland to lift the trophy and competition stalwart Hayley Turner as the last female rider to pick up the top jockey award, even if she is understating her talents ahead of raceday.

Article continues below

“To have Ryan for the first time in 20 years and to have Dylan Browne McMonagle riding for us who was champion jockey last year and who is having an incredible season this year is amazing,” she said.

“Excluding me it is probably the strongest GB and Ireland team they have ever had.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York

Joshua and Fury signed to fight in the UK but Netflix want the all-British showdown moved to Madison Square Garden in New York

View Image Anthony Joshua wants to fight in the UK

Anthony Joshua will demand a king's ransom to move his fight with Tyson Fury to New York.

‌



The British heavyweights signed contracts earlier this year to meet at home in the autumn. But Netflix, who will broadcast the fight, want it staged at a time suitable for a US audience. That would have meant the first bell ringing as late as 4am if the bout was held at Wembley.

‌



The fight organisers want to stage the showdown on November 20 - a Friday - at Madison Square Garden. Joshua, 36, admitted last month that his legacy would be damaged his biggest fight was shipped abroad. And his promoter Eddie Hearn insists they are not ready to give in.

‌



Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

"I feel like me and AJ are the last two standing on a hill waving the Union Jack," he told talkSPORT. " Anthony Joshua made me insert a clause into the contract that said the fight must happen in the UK so at the moment it can't happen anywhere else. We are under a lot of pressure because it sounds like everyone has agreed they want to do the fight at Madison Square Garden, but we don't.

We want to make it so financially unviable to change the contract that they have no choice but to do it in the UK. I don't know how it's going to play out but we wouldn't have signed the contract under its terms if the fight was going to be in America, so why should we change it now?"

Article continues below

Fury's promoter Frank Warren, meanwhile, refused to be drawn on the fight's date or location. “That will be up to his Excellency (Turki Alalshikh) to announce when he is ready to announce it," he said. “No (deadline). The fighters will just need to get into training some time in September so that is what will happen in early September.

“They will be ticking over at the moment, I’m sure. I can only speak for Tyson but he is with his family. And then as soon as the date’s announced, he will get down to the serious and bring in sparring partners and prepare for the fight. I believe the fight will go on in November.”

Sports.title: Arsenal given green light to sign £30m striker after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal given green light to sign £30m striker after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal have already began to turn their attention elsewhere after missing out on Vinicius Junior, who is set to extend his Real Madrid contract

View Image Kaua Elias is on Arsenal's radar

Arsenal have reportedly ramped up their pursuit of Kaua Elias after learning that Vinicius Junior is set to sign a new deal with Real Madrid - a major blow for the Gunners, who had been quietly optimistic about pulling off a sensational move for the winger. Their interest effectively nudged Madrid into accelerating negotiations, with talks taking place this week following his return to training.

‌



Until recently, Madrid were adamant they wouldn’t revisit or improve their latest offer. That stance has now hardened further, with Jose Mourinho naming Vinicius among six 'untouchable' players this summer - a clear message that the Brazilian is completely off‑limits.

‌



While the final details of his extension are still being ironed out, all indications point to the talismanic forward staying at the Bernabeu. With that avenue now closed, Arsenal have shifted their focus to Elias, who strengthened his rising reputation on Monday by leading Shakhtar's emphatic 5-1 win over Kudrivka.

‌



Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed READ MORE :

7 transfer targets Arsenal could miss out on with Vinicius Jr set to stay at Real Madrid READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster bagged a header, a left-footed strike and a right-footed finish in a thoroughly commanding second-half performance. Arsenal were amongst the clubs present to witness Elias' impressive display, according to The Sun, with Manchester United, AC Milan and FC Porto also monitoring the striker.

Scouts from both Arsenal and United are reported to have provided 'extremely glowing evaluations' of the 20-year-old. Elias' attraction is evident - he's comfortable on both feet, commanding in aerial duels and assured in front of goal - a profile that aligns with Arsenal's recruitment strategy.

‌



The Ukrainian champions are said to value him at approximately £30million, and the expectation is that Arsenal are now considering an official offer.

The report adds that Arsenal have been tracking Elias for several weeks, with his recent hat-trick essentially providing the club with the impetus to intensify their pursuit. United, meanwhile, are also looking to bolster their attacking options this summer, especially with Joshua Zirkzee's future uncertain amid Serie A interest.

Milan and Porto remain in contention, but Arsenal and United are regarded as being in the strongest position financially - both able to trigger the player's release clause and present an attractive package.

‌



Elias himself is believed to be receptive to a switch to one of Europe's top leagues, assuming he's offered a sporting project that corresponds with his development and long-term aspirations.

Since his arrival from Fluminense in 2025, the Brazilian has registered 12 goals and three assists across 39 outings for Shakhtar - a record that's enhanced his standing as one of the most complete young attackers coming through from South America.

Sports.title: Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis
Sports.content:
Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis

Andoni Iraola has been hit with a number of defensive injuries during his first pre-season as Liverpool boss, with Tottenham defender Djed Spence touted as a potential solution

View 3 Images England and Tottenham defender has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Liverpool have no intention of pursuing a summer transfer move for Djed Spence, despite their recent injury woes.

‌



Spence, who shone for England at the World Cup, faces an uncertain Tottenham future as Roberto De Zerbi continues to overhaul his squad.

‌



Despite his brilliant performances for the Three Lions this summer, he is likely to find himself behind new signing Andy Robertson on the left and World Cup winner Pedro Porro on the right.

‌



Spurs are therefore open to offers on the 25-year-old, who they value at around £35million. Italian giants Inter and AC Milan were both linked earlier in the summer, before Anfield was touted as a possible destination.

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola has seen just two players arrive since he succeeded Arne Slot, with Jeremy Jacquet joining the squad and Spanish winger Victor Munoz.

He has also seen his first pre-season severely hampered by a number of his defenders being unable to participate through the summer.

‌



Virgil van Dijk has been easing back to fitness after his exploits with the Netherlands, Joe Gomez was injured in the first game of pre-season, while Jacquet is still yet to feature after suffering a shoulder injury for Rennes.

Conor Bradley is also still recovering from a serious knee injury, leaving fans seriously concerned ahead of the season opener in just over a fortnight.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has seen his first pre-season hampered by defensive injuries (Image: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock)

‌



A move for the versatile Spence, who is equally adept on the left and right, appeared to tick a lot of boxes. But the ECHO understands that he is not under consideration and furthermore, the Reds have ‘absolutely no intention’ of making a move for him during the window.

Despite their mounting injury worries, it is suggested that Liverpool are not currently assessing the market for any defensive reinforcements.

Instead, the Reds are prioritising a move for an attacking player as they look to fill the vast void left after Mohamed Salah's departure.

‌



Bradley Barcola has been the big name linked for most of the summer, but Paris Saint-Germain are holding out for more than £100m for the France international.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola (R) and Ibrahim Mbaye are both wanted by Liverpool (Image: Getty)

In recent days, Barcola’s PSG team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye has emerged as an alternative to Barcola. The teenage winger could be available for a much lower fee and perhaps more importantly could be allowed to leave the European champions.

‌



Liverpool bosses are continuing to leave their options open in the forward department, with a host of names still under consideration.

Brighton's Yankiba Minteh, Said El Mala of Koln and Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo are other attackers understood to have been looked at by Anfield bosses.

The Reds have two more friendlies, firstly against Monaco on Sunday and then Como the weekend after, before they kick off their Premier League campaign against Newcastle on August 23.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher hijacks FIFA's Gianni Infantino announcement with 'bribery' dig
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher hijacks FIFA's Gianni Infantino announcement with 'bribery' dig

Jamie Carragher refused to hold his tongue as FIFA announced their decision on the future of Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency following waves of backlash for controversial World Cup plans

View Image Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Jamie Carragher's sarcastic response to FIFA's recent announcement regarding Gianni Infantino's future as World Football's president garnered far more support than the organisation's initial post. The 56-year-old has come under waves of criticism as of recent off the back of a cagey World Cup in North America, as well as controversial plans for the future of the tournament.

‌



Just last week, Infantino announced proposals dubbed the FIFA Forward Enterprise - which would have seen stakes in the World Cup sold off to private investors, should it have been successful. Instead, it was ultimately stopped dead in its tracks in an instant.

‌



Not only did football fans worldwide revolt at the idea of further monetizing what is supposed to be football's most prestigious tournament, but UEFA threatened to boycott the World Cup entirely from an ethical standpoint. As a result, FIFA quickly put the plans on the backburner, with Infantino playing them off as a consultatory process.

‌



Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS READ MORE :

Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

A statement from the FIFA president read: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

"And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve.

‌



"As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support."

Following talks, FIFA announced that their management board had put continued faith in Infantino.

A statement read: "FIFA leadership holds constructive and positive meeting in Rabat, Morocco. The FIFA Secretary General and members of the FIFA Management Board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations.

"In turn, the FIFA President reiterated his full support for the FIFA Secretary General and the FIFA Administration for their necessary and outstanding work in the delivery of his vision."

‌



Liverpool legend Carragher, who has since moved into the world of football punditry, was less than impressed by the copy, taking to X to share a GIF of Sepp Blatter infamously having money thrown at him by Simon Brodkin in 2015.

Speaking on the Football Ramble podcast, Carragher said: "I had a little chat with Arsene Wenger. He was getting involved with FIFA and it was all around this World Cup being every two years. He said, 'I'd like you to come on this other call with other ex-players and we're going to chat about the ideas going forward.' I'm like, 'Brilliant, amazing'.

‌



"We get on this Zoom and it wasn't just English players. It was like [Javier] Mascherano, there were foreign players from all over the world. They're basically talking about the pros of a World Cup every two years. I'm just listening, asking questions. I don't like the idea.

"We finish this Zoom. I haven't said whether I don't like it or it shouldn't happen, I'm just chatting with these ex players. And the guy who was organising the Zoom, then text me and said, 'Okay, can you put this out?' - like supporting it. I was like, 'No, no, no.'

"Just because I came on the Zoom...I don't agree with and I don't want it. I think it's rubbish. This feeling of, 'Once you're in here with us and you're on this Zoom, we're all these ex-players and we're in..

"That was my insight into it with Wenger and Infantino above him, with getting all these ex players in and like, 'This makes us look okay.' Half of these ex players, they don't care. From that, I was like, 'I'm not having this at all.'"

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS

UEFA previously announced plans to boycott future World Cups in the wake of Gianni Infantino's botched plans to sell off stakes in FIFA tournaments to private investors

View 2 Images FIFA chief Gianni Infantino is still under significant pressure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA have dropped a bombshell on Gianni Infantino by confirming their boycott of future tournaments still stands, with the beleaguered FIFA chief clinging onto his position.

‌



Infantino was forced to withdraw plans to sell off future FIFA tournaments to private investors following a furious backlash from football federation's, the vast majority of whom condemned the plans. UEFA provided the strongest rebuttal, insisting it's nations would boycott the next World Cup if the plans were not abandoned.

‌



And they have reaffirmed that European nations will not participate in FIFA's events if their conditions following the scandal are not met, including assurances that such a plot would never be concocted again, after it emerged Infantino retained the 'full sport' of FIFA's board on Wednesday night.

‌



A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up READ MORE :

Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges READ MORE :

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

‌



"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

View 2 Images UEFA are still preparing to boycott future World Cups (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

UEFA's latest public attack on Infantino means the significant heat which has been on the Swiss executive in recent weeks is unlikely to subside anytime soon.

‌



Shortly after UEFA's statement was released, the English Football Association officially sent its letter withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election, potentially opening the floodgates for other major nations to follow.

Although UEFA were the only confederation to threaten a complete boycott of FIFA tournaments, Concacaf and the Asian Football Federation also rejected Infantino's plans. Concacaf were the only other confederation to publicly question Infantino, though.

Infantino apologised for "mistakes" in a letter addressing the botched plans, which would have seen national federations bank £30.1million courtesy of the FIFA Forward Enterprise.

Sports.title: Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money
Sports.content:
Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money

Jamie Carragher has said he was surprised by the Liverpool legend's switch to Trabzonspor but Super Lig clubs are spending big and attracting some top talent

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor (Image: OZAN KOSE, AFP via Getty Images)

As usual, Jamie Carragher makes a very valid point when he suggests that Mohamed Salah is still good enough to be playing in a competition of a higher standard than the Turkish Süper Lig.

‌



Salah is certainly good enough to still be a major performer in the Champions League but will have to be content with playing in the Europa League next season, assuming Trabzonspor negotiates the qualifying round.

‌



Let’s face it, Salah is still good enough to be playing in the Premier League but you can assume that prospect was contractually removed when the player and Liverpool agreed to part ways a year early. Anyway, Salah probably could not countenance playing for another Premier League club. Not yet, anyway.

‌



But there must have been interest from some blue-chip Champions League clubs in a 34-year-old all-time Premier League great who, by his standards, had an average time of things last season but was still one of Liverpool’s better performers. Which is why the obvious conclusion is that Trabzonspor are paying fantastic wages.

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

That will certainly be the case. The marquee Turkish clubs - Istanbul’s big three, Galatasary, Fenerbahce and Besiktas, plus Trabzonspor - are spending big on players and contracts despite being burdened with heavy debt.

Salah will be playing in a league that will feature the likes of Victor Osimhen, Leroy Sane, Ilkay Gundogan, Leandro Trossard and Nathan Ake this coming season. And there will probably be more to follow.

‌



But it will take many more recruits of that quality to make Turkish club football a major force in European football. Since Galatasaray won the UEFA Cup in 2000, only one Turkish side has reached the semi-finals of a major UEFA competition.

View 3 Images Leandro Trossard left Arsenal for Besiktas earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Opta currently ranks it as the 14th strongest domestic league in world football, behind national competitions in countries such as Denmark and Poland. According to Opta, England’s Championship is stronger.

‌



That would seem to be stretching it a little but there is no doubt, of course, that Salah is taking a significantly-sized step backwards in terms of the overall quality of the league he is operating in. But aside from the considerable financial attraction - his deal is said to be worth around £14million a year - perhaps Salah just wanted a different experience.

For sure, the Premier League is ultra-competitive and generates enormous interest. Stadiums are full and it is a commercial behemoth.

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah was greeted by thousands of Trabzonspor fans when he arrived at the airport (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



But sometimes, it feels a little bit too sanitised, a little bit too polished, a little bit too commercial. Tunnel clubs for wealthy fans, hospitality takeovers. And to be honest, even on the pitch, everything has become a little sanitised. Very good but not as edgy as it once was.

Perhaps Salah fancied something a little more visceral, a little more unpredictable, a little more volatile (a lot more volatile), a little more raw. He might have just fancied the cash, of course, but maybe that was not the be-all and end-all.

Yes, you might have expected him to rock up in Serie A but he has made a fascinating decision late in his career. And it will be fascinating to see how it works out.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
